questions.stem: A patient with asthma is tachypneic and has an early respiratory alkalosis. Later, the patient's breathing becomes ineffective and carbon dioxide rises. What best explains the later change?

options.text: Airflow obstruction limits carbon dioxide elimination
Renal loss of bicarbonate causes metabolic alkalosis
Fibrin dissolves in the pulmonary circulation
Erythropoietin secretion increases

questions.rationale: Worsening obstruction can impair ventilation and lead to carbon dioxide retention and respiratory acidosis.
questions.draftNote: Unreviewed addition; requires source and semantic duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient with a large pulmonary embolism develops signs of right ventricular strain. Which change most directly increases the ventricle's workload?

options.text: Increased resistance in pulmonary circulation
Reduced systemic blood viscosity
Increased filtration through the kidneys
Decreased pressure in pulmonary arteries

questions.rationale: Obstruction and hypoxic vasoconstriction raise pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular workload.
questions.draftNote: Unreviewed addition; requires source and semantic duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient with a prior gastric bypass reports fatigue and tingling in the feet. Which anemia should the nurse consider?

options.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia
Iron deficiency anemia as the only possible explanation
Polycythemia
Thrombocytosis

questions.rationale: The worksheet links gastric bypass to impaired B12 absorption and identifies paresthesias with B12 deficiency.
questions.draftNote: Unreviewed addition; requires source and semantic duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient with dysuria and urgency subsequently develops fever and costovertebral angle tenderness. What does the change suggest?

options.text: Infection may have ascended to the kidneys
The infection is now limited to the urethral opening
A pulmonary artery is obstructed
A factor VIII deficiency has developed

questions.rationale: Fever and costovertebral angle tenderness support possible upper urinary tract involvement.
questions.draftNote: Unreviewed addition; requires source and semantic duplicate review.

questions.stem: A patient with advanced CKD develops hyperkalemia and peaked T waves after missed dialysis. Which problem should the nurse recognize?

options.text: Reduced potassium removal with a risk of cardiac effects
Excess potassium excretion is causing hypokalemia
The kidneys are producing excess erythropoietin
Vitamin B12 is directly occluding the ureters

questions.rationale: Advanced kidney dysfunction reduces potassium excretion; the quiz links missed dialysis and peaked T waves with hyperkalemia.
